# Sawaliya Food Products Limited | SME deep research

Framework v3.0 · Universe position 358 · Information frozen 20 October 2026 · Market reference 19 October 2026

## 1. Executive Verdict

**Hold — unresolved financial reliability and funding evidence.** Sawaliya is a small B 2 B dehydrated-vegetable manufacturer with genuine historical volume growth and institutional customers, not an evidenced consumer-brand compounder. Revenue reached ₹41.31 crore in FY2026, but reported operating cash was only ₹0.125 crore against ₹8.005 crore PAT. The decisive issue is whether profits and receivables become usable cash after settling obligations, not the headline growth rate. Revised H 1 earnings, incomplete loan/cash reconciliations and delayed IPO-funded commissioning prevent a dependable normalized earnings or intrinsic-value estimate at the verified ₹184.50 close. This is a cash-conversion/expansion special-situation research candidate, not an eligible investment recommendation. Full reconciliations, subsequent collections, usable bank funding and commissioned capacity would change the assessment. No substantiated fraud or actual default is alleged. ([results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 6–16; [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–156)

## 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit

GQS means **Growth Quality Score**, not governance; governance is GOV. Integer factors are assigned once and reused. NS means not scoreable, ND means not disclosed/located, NM means not meaningful, and NA is reserved for genuine inapplicability.

| Factor | Score | Confidence | Why / evidence |

| GOV | 4 | Medium | Recurring reporting/control and deployment shortcomings; not a substantiated diversion finding. AU08, AU10, AU11, AU12, AU16, AU18, AU20, E05, E06 |
| MOAT | 4 | Medium | Useful quality/process relationships but contestable ingredient economics, concentration and no demonstrated pricing moat. E01, E02, E03 |
| REV | 8 | Medium | Five-year original operating-revenue CAGR sets starting 8; zero trajectory adjustment. Medium confidence/history quality ceiling 8. E01, E03, E04, AU18 |
| DUR | 5 | Medium | Accessible institutional ingredient demand and plant capability, constrained by concentration, procurement seasonality and delayed expansion. E01, E02, E07 |
| CAP | NS | Low | Incremental sustainable returns not scoreable until profit/capital classifications and commissioning settle. E04, E05, E06, E07, AU14 |
| CASH | 2 | Medium | Persistent poor realization over profitable years, not capex as an excuse for CFO. E04, E05, AU14, AU18 |
| BAL | NS | Low | Current accessible cash, claim timing, bank limits and loan recovery insufficiently verified. E05, E06, AU13, AU20 |
| EXEC | 4 | Medium | Operational scaling is real but dated IPO delivery and disclosure commitments were missed. E03, E07, E08 |
| EARN | NS | Low | True sustainable profit growth cannot be separated confidently from inventory/tax/finance reclassifications. E04, E05, AU18 |
| R | NS | Low | Conditional model is not a reliable current base return: opening liquidity and normalized earnings are unresolved. E09, MODEL |
| D | 3 | Medium | Material impairment vulnerability in concentrated debt-funded receivables/inventory model. E05, E06, E11, MODEL |
| P | NS | Low | Purchase-price buffer cannot be measured against a dependable intrinsic-value range. E09, MODEL |
| L | 6 | Medium | Starting 9 from 1.0034 theoretical days; explicit 3-point implementation downgrade, not an invented turnover shortage. E09, E10 |

| Measure | Raw point | Raw missing bounds | Override | Final | Final bounds | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BQS | NS | 3.78–5.58 | None; critical hold | NS | 3.78–5.58 | 80.00% |
| GQS | NS | 4.70–7.40 | Cap 5 | NS | 4.70–5.00 | 70.00% |
| IAS | NS | 1.90–8.20 | None; critical hold | NS | 1.90–8.20 | 30.00% |

**BQS**: GOV 4 × .20 = 0.80; MOAT 4 × .20 = 0.80; REV 8 × .12 = 0.96; DUR 5 × .10 = 0.50; CAP NS × .12 = NS; CASH 2 × .10 = 0.20; BAL NS × .08 = NS; EXEC 4 × .08 = 0.32. Known contribution 3.58.

**GQS**: REV 8 × .40 = 3.20; DUR 5 × .20 = 1.00; EARN NS × .15 = NS; CAP NS × .15 = NS; CASH 2 × .10 = 0.20. Known contribution 4.40.

**IAS**: BQS NS × .25 = NS; R NS × .35 = NS; D 3 × .20 = 0.60; P NS × .10 = NS; L 6 × .10 = 0.60. Known contribution 1.20.

All arithmetic uses Decimal precision 32. One-decimal display uses half-up rounding; classification uses unrounded values. Missing weights are not renormalized. The raw bounds are mathematical possibilities for missing factors, not confidence intervals, fair values or ranking points. IAS's ordinary missing-data bound is 1.900–8.200; propagating the narrower BQS missing-data bounds yields 2.595–7.095. Both remain NS under the critical hold.

The only numeric override applied is the GQS ceiling 5, because CASH 2 reflects repeated weak realization, not one capex year. It does not turn NS into 5. There is no governance override (GOV 4, no evidenced G1 failure) or funding cap (G3 unresolved, not proven failure). GOV±1 changes known BQS contribution±0.20; DUR±1 changes BQS±0.10 and GQS±0.20. Together BQS bounds shift±0.30; no midpoint or spurious upgrade results. L starts 9 from the prescribed capacity test, then loses 2 for dated irregular-trading/low-PAN warnings and 1 for lot/ownership concentration plus unobserved executable depth. There is no further hidden haircut. [judgment/evidence ledger E01–E11, AU01–AU21]

## 4. Business Overview

Incorporated in 2014, Sawaliya processes dehydrated carrot cubes, cabbage and ring beans used in noodles, pasta, soups and other packaged foods. Customers are institutional manufacturers, domestic traders and US importers. FY2025 institutional revenue was ₹22.61 crore (66.15%), trader revenue ₹10.67 crore (31.22%) and exports ₹0.90 crore (2.63%). Exports were only to the US in the disclosed period, not a diversified global franchise. Madhya Pradesh represented 76.70% of FY2025 sales and 95.57% of raw procurement, adding geographic/procurement concentration. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–146)

The FY2025 product table contains ₹10.52 crore carrot-A cubes, ₹10.43 crore ring beans, ₹5.34 crore cabbage and smaller dehydrated lines. Washed carrots ₹3.98 crore, wheat powder ₹2.07 crore and dextrose ₹0.034 crore mean headline sales are not all manufactured dehydrated tonnage. Customer counts rose 12→84→91 in FY2023–25, but FY2024's increase partly reflected washed-carrot traders rather than equivalent sticky institutional contracts. Direct farmer procurement and product specifications can support service quality, but managerial cost-advantage claims are not proof of a structural moat. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–151)

The economic cycle is seasonal procurement, conversion/drying/cold storage, sale and collection. Stocks, supplier advances and long customer credit absorb funds before profit becomes cash. The RHP explicitly discusses earlier working-capital shortages and supplier payment delays, and later trader credit expansion. Cash realization, yields, rejection rates, energy cost, spoilage and credit losses matter as much as selling-price growth. Company-specific yield, rejection and energy-per-tonne histories are ND. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 28–35,138–156)

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

Relationships, food specifications, consistent batches, storage and proximity to procurement are useful capabilities. Output growth supports actual commercial traction. However, the principal West Bengal FMCG customer is not named in the relevant disclosure and has a 10–12-month renewable contract; blanket purchase orders from others do not guarantee quantities. No famous customer is inferred. Repeat key-customer sales were 52.12% in FY2025 versus 92.82% in FY2023. The top 10 customers contributed ₹29.70 crore: the RHP's 86.50% uses total income ₹34.3384 crore; against operating revenue the concentration is **86.89%**. The largest customer is 20.76% of operating sales. Top 10 suppliers represent 73.07% of purchases, the largest 34.36%. Counterparty names/connectedness beyond disclosed relationships are not independently established. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 29–31,138–146)

FY2020 is a comparative in the FY2021 audited statement, not a separately reviewed FY2020 audit. Original FY2020/21 operations ₹5.4043/₹11.2414 crore differ from aggregator values ₹5.29/₹10.82 crore; the original lines are retained. Six observations support the five-year CAGR. Ten-year CAGR is ND, not extrapolated. The record is one legal operating perimeter, but acquisitions being absent does not make price/mix irrelevant. ([AR21](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Annual-Report_2020-21.pdf), PDF 12; [AR22](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Annual-Report_2021-22.pdf), PDF 14; [AR23](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Annual-Report_2022-23.pdf), PDF 13; [AR24](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SFPPL-FInancials-23-24.pdf), PDF 14; [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 198; [results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 6)

Manufacturing production rose 730.84→1,107.5→1,325 MT in FY2023–25, a two-year 34.65% CAGR. Capacity expanded 950→1,500 MT and then stayed 1,500 MT; FY2025 utilization is 88.33% from raw values. FY2025 volume increased 19.64% while revenue increased 46.10%, showing price/product/trading mix contributed. The RHP prints 88.00% total utilization, while 1,325/1,500=88.33%; some category utilization percentages also fail their numerator/denominator checks. The early FY2023/24 institutional-mix histories on PDF 139 and 143 conflict, and FY2024 washed-carrot sales are ₹609.51 lakh on PDF 31 but a dash in the PDF 144 product cell despite the same total revenue. These conflicts preclude an exact clean price/volume/trading bridge; FY2025 institutional figures agree. Total utilization is recalculated rather than copied. FY2026 volumes and segment mix are ND; its revenue grew 20.84%, not a one-quarter annualization. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 151–156; [results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 6)

REV 8 uses the five-year CAGR's 20–30% starting band with zero trajectory adjustment. Manufacturing volume is a cross-check that expansion was not only pricing. A Medium confidence ceiling of 8 applies despite longer legal history because current mix and financial reliability remain imperfect. There is not enough clean repeated post-IPO period evidence to add or subtract another trajectory point. REV does not score projected capacity, margins, TAM or valuation. If later records show the revenue basis materially distorted, REV must become NS or be rescored, not defended by its historical percentage.

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

Current physical capacity is modest, and the manufacturing base is already fairly utilized. Growth can come from greater throughput, wider product mix, repeat institutional orders and funded new equipment. The relevant accessible opportunity is contracts that can be supplied and collected, not an unsourced national TAM. The RHP proposed machinery plus 149.04 kWp solar for ₹7.4866 crore and described 370 MT of FY2027 production capacity in wording that also says installed capacity remains unchanged. The model therefore treats 370 MT as a **conditional effective increment**, with a zero-increment sensitivity, not an established 1,870 MT nameplate. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 95–105,151–156)

Commissioning was planned for 15 December 2025. By 30 May 2026, equipment delivery and installation timing remained uncertain because of cited Gulf-route disruptions. ₹4.7382 crore was reported used for capex, with ₹2.7484 crore left. Paid advances are committed capital, not usable cash or already productive plant. The recorded capital advance/CWIP plus remaining cash exceeds the original capex object by ₹0.1200 crore under the model allocation, explicitly an assumption requiring reconciliation. ([results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 12–16)

| Year / basis | ONWC ₹cr | IC ₹cr | Finance-side ₹cr | Residual ₹lakh | ROIC accounting proxy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 7.35 | 15.35 | 15.35 | 0.010 | ND |

| 2025 | 29.38 | 37.59 | 37.59 | -0.010 | 31.17% |

For FY2023–25, ONWC includes operating supplier advances and security deposits/prepayments, excludes tax/IPO financing assets and cash, and subtracts operating payables. IC includes CWIP, not only commissioned PPE. Finance-side IC adds debt, tax provisions and deferred tax to equity and subtracts non-operating assets; residuals are shown. ₹65.56 lakh FY2023 and ₹131 lakh FY2024 capital subsidies were deducted from asset cost, reducing reported capital and depreciation. A gross-of-subsidy capital diagnostic is retained, but is not a reconstructed gross replacement-value balance sheet. FY2026 classification is too coarse for comparable ROIC; a broad asset/finance reconciliation is shown without awarding CAP. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 197–212, especially PDF 210–211)

The FY2023–25 two-year endpoint NOPAT/IC-change proxy is 34.93%. Three- and five-year comparable incremental returns are NS/ND, not extraordinarily high estimates derived from a thin or inconsistent denominator. Margin improvement on old plant, subsidies, trading mix, advances and immature projects prevent attributing profit growth to new capital. The analysis compares possible post-tax returns with a 14–18% nominal INR cost-of-capital range, not a universal threshold. GQS remains NS, bounded and capped, because strong revenue growth has not yet earned reliable returns and cash conversion.

## 8. Management, Governance & Execution

Raghav Somani is the managing director in the reviewed filings. Family control aligns some incentives but is not proof of minority protection. FY2025 director remuneration ₹36.80 lakh plus relatives' salaries ₹60 lakh equaled 14.32% of original PAT. Related-party borrowing outstanding was about ₹397 lakh versus ₹118.72 lakh FY2024; this is financing support, not automatically outward leakage. The company describes transactions as ordinary-course/arm's-length and CARO reports compliance with Sections 177/188. No related-party sales/purchases line was disclosed in the reviewed note, which is not equivalent to proving no such transaction existed. ([AR25](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28692_SAWALIYA_2024_2025_A_3544664_05092025212518.pdf), PDF 29,56; [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), related-party note)

Original auditor Nirza Gattani resigned 20 July 2024 citing preoccupation; Maheshwari & Gupta was appointed 21 July and subsequently for a five-year term. This is a disclosed reason, not an unexplained disappearance. Priya Somani resigned as whole-time director on 8 May 2026 for personal reasons and confirmed no other material reason; no adverse motive is inferred. ([AR25](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28692_SAWALIYA_2024_2025_A_3544664_05092025212518.pdf); [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 194–196; [resignation](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Outcome-of-BM_08.05.2026_signed.pdf), PDF 1–3)

| RHP machinery commercial production 15 Dec 2025; solar 10 Sep 2025 | May 2026 installation date uncertain; capex object 63.29% utilized | Execution weakness; logistics explanation is relevant but does not make capacity productive |
| IPO loan repayment ₹461.15 lakh | ₹81.09 lakh used, ₹380.06 lakh left; March 24 bank request pending | Do not assume prepayment occurred; management says regular EMIs continued |

The statutory overall FY2025 opinion and IFC opinion were unmodified. Older originals also require care: FY2022/23 IFC opinion paragraphs retain 31 March 2021 dates despite current-year scope/signature; FY2024 references AnnexureB, which was not present in the supplied 31-page packet. Original annual cash-flow statements were not located, including FY2024/25 despite references in audit scope. These are document/reporting limitations, not a claim that the overall audit opinions were qualified. Nonetheless, CARO's internal-audit wording, contradictory no-term-loan/no-CWIP statements despite notes showing both, old unconfirmed balances and tax arrears warrant GOV 4. The ₹135.17468 lakh undisputed overdue income-tax amount is **not** the same as five small disputed direct-tax cases totaling about ₹1.35 lakh. Neither is automatically fraud. Terminal FCFF is earned after replacement/growth capital, incremental working capital and operating cash requirements. ## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

**Permanent-capital-impairment risk: High.** This is a qualitative vulnerability assessment consistent with D 3, concentrated working assets, uncertain recoverability and funding dependence, not a quantified probability or an allegation that loss has already occurred. IPO equity and reported positive EBIT prevent treating severe failure as established.

The strongest bear case is not simply slowing growth. A concentrated buyer delays payment or reduces orders; finished-goods stock becomes slow-moving; procurement still requires advances; plant utilization falls and margins compress; already secured receivables/inventory support less new bank credit; obligations and capex continue before collections; an equity issue becomes dilutive or unavailable. Recovery of loans to others cannot be presumed. This links operating deterioration, capital intensity, bank collateral and per-share impairment rather than applying an arbitrary valuation haircut.

The single thesis-break variable is **verified cash realization of reported receivables and advances after satisfying prior claims**. A persistently growing debtor/loan balance with no supported collection or financing bridge would invalidate the expansion thesis even if reported sales and PAT rise. Proven diversion or falsified accounts would separately trigger G1 failure, but that has not been established.

The strongest counterevidence is real historic manufacturing output growth, positive reported EBIT, a substantial post-IPO equity buffer, debt reduction, some inventory release, improved creditor ageing and unmodified audit/IFC/no-default statements. These prevent presenting the adverse case as certainty. The market may already discount small-company liquidity and cash risks; no informational edge or market mispricing is claimed without evidence.

## 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action

**Hold — unresolved**, with BQS NS, GQS NS and IAS NS. Even the supported-arithmetic, conditional base paths produce negative 5/10-year returns and the bull 10-year path remains below the 15% hurdle at the reference price; these are conservative laboratory outcomes, not forecasts. The numeric classification matrix cannot manufacture a point where critical factors are missing. Pending-evidence placement is separate from a low-quality bottom rank and from an evidenced governance/default exclusion. GOV 4/MOAT 4/CASH 2, missing CAP and the holds also fail the evidence-backed compounder criteria, irrespective of historical growth.

Action category: **Research hold / pending evidence**, not “buy after a small price fall.” Priority is to obtain reconciled original cash/earnings statements, current bank/loan confirmations, subsequent collections and actual commissioning. If those become reliable, rebuild every linked path, rescore affected canonical factors once and apply the unrounded matrix. If they establish actual abuse or unfinanceable default, apply the specified overrides. If the business proves sound but the price changes alone, update IAS without reflexively changing BQS/GQS. No portfolio allocation, trading instruction, Git publication or batch ranking change is implied by this record.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: **Hold — unresolved financial reliability and funding evidence.** Sawaliya is a small B 2 B dehydrated-vegetable manufacturer with genuine historical volume growth and institutional customers, not an evidenced consumer-brand compounder. Revenue reached ₹41.31 crore in FY2026, but reported operating cash was only ₹0.125 crore against ₹8.005 crore PAT. The decisive issue is whether profits and receivables become usable cash after settling obligations, not the headline growth rate. Revised H 1 earnings, incomplete loan/cash reconciliations and delayed IPO-funded commissioning prevent a dependable normalized earnings or intrinsic-value estimate at the verified ₹184.50 close. This is a cash-conversion/expansion special-situation research candidate, not an eligible investment recommendation. Full reconciliations, subsequent collections, usable bank funding and commissioned capacity would change the assessment. No substantiated fraud or actual default is alleged. ([results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 6–16; [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–156)

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Incorporated in 2014, Sawaliya processes dehydrated carrot cubes, cabbage and ring beans used in noodles, pasta, soups and other packaged foods. Customers are institutional manufacturers, domestic traders and US importers. FY2025 institutional revenue was ₹22.61 crore (66.15%), trader revenue ₹10.67 crore (31.22%) and exports ₹0.90 crore (2.63%). Exports were only to the US in the disclosed period, not a diversified global franchise. Madhya Pradesh represented 76.70% of FY2025 sales and 95.57% of raw procurement, adding geographic/procurement concentration. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–146)

The FY2025 product table contains ₹10.52 crore carrot-A cubes, ₹10.43 crore ring beans, ₹5.34 crore cabbage and smaller dehydrated lines. Washed carrots ₹3.98 crore, wheat powder ₹2.07 crore and dextrose ₹0.034 crore mean headline sales are not all manufactured dehydrated tonnage. Customer counts rose 12→84→91 in FY2023–25, but FY2024's increase partly reflected washed-carrot traders rather than equivalent sticky institutional contracts. Direct farmer procurement and product specifications can support service quality, but managerial cost-advantage claims are not proof of a structural moat. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 138–151)

The economic cycle is seasonal procurement, conversion/drying/cold storage, sale and collection. Stocks, supplier advances and long customer credit absorb funds before profit becomes cash. The RHP explicitly discusses earlier working-capital shortages and supplier payment delays, and later trader credit expansion. Cash realization, yields, rejection rates, energy cost, spoilage and credit losses matter as much as selling-price growth. Company-specific yield, rejection and energy-per-tonne histories are ND. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 28–35,138–156)

sections.content_markdown:
Relationships, food specifications, consistent batches, storage and proximity to procurement are useful capabilities. Output growth supports actual commercial traction. However, the principal West Bengal FMCG customer is not named in the relevant disclosure and has a 10–12-month renewable contract; blanket purchase orders from others do not guarantee quantities. No famous customer is inferred. Repeat key-customer sales were 52.12% in FY2025 versus 92.82% in FY2023. The top 10 customers contributed ₹29.70 crore: the RHP's 86.50% uses total income ₹34.3384 crore; against operating revenue the concentration is **86.89%**. The largest customer is 20.76% of operating sales. Top 10 suppliers represent 73.07% of purchases, the largest 34.36%. sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
Current physical capacity is modest, and the manufacturing base is already fairly utilized. Growth can come from greater throughput, wider product mix, repeat institutional orders and funded new equipment. The relevant accessible opportunity is contracts that can be supplied and collected, not an unsourced national TAM. The RHP proposed machinery plus 149.04 kWp solar for ₹7.4866 crore and described 370 MT of FY2027 production capacity in wording that also says installed capacity remains unchanged. The model therefore treats 370 MT as a **conditional effective increment**, with a zero-increment sensitivity, not an established 1,870 MT nameplate. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 95–105,151–156)

Commissioning was planned for 15 December 2025. By 30 May 2026, equipment delivery and installation timing remained uncertain because of cited Gulf-route disruptions. ₹4.7382 crore was reported used for capex, with ₹2.7484 crore left. Paid advances are committed capital, not usable cash or already productive plant. The recorded capital advance/CWIP plus remaining cash exceeds the original capex object by ₹0.1200 crore under the model allocation, explicitly an assumption requiring reconciliation. ([results 26](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SAWALIYA_30052026191417_Outcome.pdf), PDF 12–16)

Finance-side IC adds debt, tax provisions and deferred tax to equity and subtracts non-operating assets; residuals are shown. ₹65.56 lakh FY2023 and ₹131 lakh FY2024 capital subsidies were deducted from asset cost, reducing reported capital and depreciation. A gross-of-subsidy capital diagnostic is retained, but is not a reconstructed gross replacement-value balance sheet. FY2026 classification is too coarse for comparable ROIC; a broad asset/finance reconciliation is shown without awarding CAP. ([rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 197–212, especially PDF 210–211)

The FY2023–25 two-year endpoint NOPAT/IC-change proxy is 34.93%. Three- and five-year comparable incremental returns are NS/ND, not extraordinarily high estimates derived from a thin or inconsistent denominator. Margin improvement on old plant, subsidies, trading mix, advances and immature projects prevent attributing profit growth to new capital. The analysis compares possible post-tax returns with a 14–18% nominal INR cost-of-capital range, not a universal threshold. GQS remains NS, bounded and capped, because strong revenue growth has not yet earned reliable returns and cash conversion.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
Raghav Somani is the managing director in the reviewed filings. Family control aligns some incentives but is not proof of minority protection. FY2025 director remuneration ₹36.80 lakh plus relatives' salaries ₹60 lakh equaled 14.32% of original PAT. Related-party borrowing outstanding was about ₹397 lakh versus ₹118.72 lakh FY2024; this is financing support, not automatically outward leakage. The company describes transactions as ordinary-course/arm's-length and CARO reports compliance with Sections 177/188. No related-party sales/purchases line was disclosed in the reviewed note, which is not equivalent to proving no such transaction existed. ([AR25](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28692_SAWALIYA_2024_2025_A_3544664_05092025212518.pdf), PDF 29,56; [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), related-party note)

Original auditor Nirza Gattani resigned 20 July 2024 citing preoccupation; Maheshwari & Gupta was appointed 21 July and subsequently for a five-year term. This is a disclosed reason, not an unexplained disappearance. Priya Somani resigned as whole-time director on 8 May 2026 for personal reasons and confirmed no other material reason; no adverse motive is inferred. ([AR25](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28692_SAWALIYA_2024_2025_A_3544664_05092025212518.pdf); [rhp](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sawaliya-RHP.pdf), PDF 194–196; [resignation](https://sawaliyafood.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Outcome-of-BM_08.05.2026_signed.pdf), PDF 1–3)

The statutory overall FY2025 opinion and IFC opinion were unmodified. Older originals also require care: FY2022/23 IFC opinion paragraphs retain 31 March 2021 dates despite current-year scope/signature; FY2024 references AnnexureB, which was not present in the supplied 31-page packet. Original annual cash-flow statements were not located, including FY2024/25 despite references in audit scope. These are document/reporting limitations, not a claim that the overall audit opinions were qualified. Nonetheless, CARO's internal-audit wording, contradictory no-term-loan/no-CWIP statements despite notes showing both, old unconfirmed balances and tax arrears warrant GOV 4. The ₹135.17468 lakh undisputed overdue income-tax amount is **not** the same as five small disputed direct-tax cases totaling about ₹1.35 lakh. Neither is automatically fraud. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
**Permanent-capital-impairment risk: High.** This is a qualitative vulnerability assessment consistent with D 3, concentrated working assets, uncertain recoverability and funding dependence, not a quantified probability or an allegation that loss has already occurred. IPO equity and reported positive EBIT prevent treating severe failure as established.

The strongest bear case is not simply slowing growth. A concentrated buyer delays payment or reduces orders; finished-goods stock becomes slow-moving; procurement still requires advances; plant utilization falls and margins compress; already secured receivables/inventory support less new bank credit; obligations and capex continue before collections; an equity issue becomes dilutive or unavailable. Recovery of loans to others cannot be presumed. This links operating deterioration, capital intensity, bank collateral and per-share impairment rather than applying an arbitrary valuation haircut.

The single thesis-break variable is **verified cash realization of reported receivables and advances after satisfying prior claims**. A persistently growing debtor/loan balance with no supported collection or financing bridge would invalidate the expansion thesis even if reported sales and PAT rise. Proven diversion or falsified accounts would separately trigger G1 failure, but that has not been established.

The strongest counterevidence is real historic manufacturing output growth, positive reported EBIT, a substantial post-IPO equity buffer, debt reduction, some inventory release, improved creditor ageing and unmodified audit/IFC/no-default statements. These prevent presenting the adverse case as certainty. The market may already discount small-company liquidity and cash risks; no informational edge or market mispricing is claimed without evidence.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved**, with BQS NS, GQS NS and IAS NS. Even the supported-arithmetic, conditional base paths produce negative 5/10-year returns and the bull 10-year path remains below the 15% hurdle at the reference price; these are conservative laboratory outcomes, not forecasts. The numeric classification matrix cannot manufacture a point where critical factors are missing. Pending-evidence placement is separate from a low-quality bottom rank and from an evidenced governance/default exclusion. GOV 4/MOAT 4/CASH 2, missing CAP and the holds also fail the evidence-backed compounder criteria, irrespective of historical growth.

Action category: **Research hold / pending evidence**, not “buy after a small price fall.” Priority is to obtain reconciled original cash/earnings statements, current bank/loan confirmations, subsequent collections and actual commissioning. If those become reliable, rebuild every linked path, rescore affected canonical factors once and apply the unrounded matrix. If they establish actual abuse or unfinanceable default, apply the specified overrides. If the business proves sound but the price changes alone, update IAS without reflexively changing BQS/GQS. No portfolio allocation, trading instruction, Git publication or batch ranking change is implied by this record.
